subject: Tenant demarcation, egress attenuation & fallback playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: alex.brown@acmecorp.com, ops-eng@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant demarcation and egress attenuation proposal v1

Grace / Irene —

Attaching the first-pass reference diagram and a short policy matrix for ACME's private deployment. This focuses on two things we agreed on in the kickoff: (1) clear control-plane vs data-plane demarcation for tenant isolation, and (2) an egress attenuation + fallback model so their on-prem workloads can keep operating when the primary outbound path is constrained.

High-level summary:
- Control plane: regionally redundant control-plane agents run in ACME's management VPC (customer-owned). They talk to Redwood's private control plane over an authenticated TLS channel (mutual TLS with client certs) to pull assignments and configs. All control-plane traffic is API-only, port 443, with strict CIDR allowlist.
- Data plane: inference runtime sits inside ACME tenant VPCs (isolated subnets). No direct inbound from Redwood; we use an outbound-initiated ephemeral session model and tokenized KV cache pre-warm to reduce cold-starts.
- Egress attenuation: per-tenant egress rate-limiter + proxy (SIDECAR or shared NAT proxy depending on capacity). Default policy: allow model-serving outbound to Redwood gateway endpoints only; deny arbitrary outbound to public internet.
- Fallback: when primary Redwood gateway is unavailable, tenant nodes route to a regional fallback endpoint that runs a reduced-capacity runtime (quantized smaller variant) hosted in ACME's cloud account under dedicated billing. This keeps P95 latency bounded while preventing data exfiltration.

Open items for ACME:
- KMS/HSM integration model (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed)
- Legal sign-off on fallback runtime (where inference artifacts live)
- Egress logging retention and SOC2 evidence formatting

Attachments: vpc-demarc-diagram-v1.pdf, egress-policy-matrix.xlsx

Pls review; I'd like to get your redlines before I share with ACME's security team tomorrow EOD.

—Jonas
Lead Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: alex.brown@acmecorp.com, ops-eng@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant demarcation and egress attenuation proposal v1

Thanks Jonas — good start. A few actionable notes before we loop in Kimberly and ACME security: 

1) Control-plane authentication: we should explicitly call out certificate rotation cadence and a short spec for cert revocation (CRL/OCSP) that ACME can implement in their PKI. Add a fallback auth token flow for emergency key rotation.

2) Data-plane isolation: call out subnet-level IAM role assumptions and the requirement that nothing in the tenant subnet has an internet-facing ELB. If ACME needs egress to specific SaaS endpoints (monitoring, metrics), we want an allowlist and a dedicated proxy tunnel — no divergence from the main outbound gateway.

3) Fallback runtime: this is the trickiest item. We need an explicit note that model weights remain encrypted at rest with customer-controlled keys if the fallback is hosted in ACME account. If fallback runs in Redwood-managed infra, we require an SLA fallback approval and a separate contract appendix.

4) Logging & evidence: define schema for egress logs (timestamp, src-instance-id, dst-host, dst-ip, allowlist-rule-id, bytes, action) and ensure we can produce CSV extracts for audits.

Can you surface these changes in the diagram and a one-page appendix? Kimberly, I'm looping you for procurement/input on the fallback commercial model (BYO vs Redwood-managed).

Grace
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Grace / team —

Thanks for the clear notes. From a compliance perspective (they asked for SOC2 + EU data residency considerations):

- CRLs/OCSP: we should require that ACME's PKI supports OCSP stapling for control-plane endpoints. Provide a 7-day max rotation window for certs used by control agents.
- Egress logging retention: default 90 days on customer side; 12 months available as an add-on. For SOC2 evidence, ensure logs can be exported with SHA256 checksum manifests.
- Fallback runtime: If customer-owned (preferred), they must run the fallback in an account that enforces envelope encryption with their KMS key. If Redwood-managed fallback is used, we must map the data classification and run a separate penetration test and SAR (security assessment report) to include in their audit pack.
- Network-level controls: recommend using BGP community tagging for route preference so that we can failover gracefully and avoid asymmetric routing during a gateway outage.

Small edits I put inline in the diagram PDF and a new worksheet with KMS options. Jonas — see the inline comments on page 2 (control-plane flow) and the new sheet 'kms-options' in egress-policy-matrix.xlsx.

Irene
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
